people.role: Head of Vụ Ẩn Môn since 1146: mist formations and concealment arrays along the cape's roads
people.appearance: A thin, grey, unremarkable man in an oiled cloak, easy to forget even when he is standing in front of you, which he has practised.
people.backstory: Bàng Yên Tỏa was a tea-picker's son from Trà Viên Thôn, the tea village south of the sect's gate. At fifteen he was hired to carry loads on the cape roads. In 1100 the founder, Hàm Thủ Lộ (ham_thu_lo), saw him walk out of a robbers' ambush on the Phù Kiều road by keeping so still that nobody looked at him, and took him in. He learned the Road Mist Primer, then the Mist-Lock canon, then the Haze Walk that Tất Hành Vụ (tat_hanh_vu) had given the founder (N-thuy_vi-07). In 1146 the founder died of age in his arms on the Đồng Sơn road, and at his wish Bàng buried him under the gate's threshold and let the cape believe the mist had taken him (N-vu_an-03). Bàng became head at sixty-one and has kept the sect small, quiet and paid. In 1190, after the band killed Bối Trường Đình (boi_truong_dinh), he went to Thúy Vi's Hall of Rules for patrols, and has paid for them since with pages. In 1198 a frost heave cracked the threshold, and the founder's daughter found out what he had kept from her. Tất still visits every spring, and the elders who call the walk a theft still talk of a tithe.
people.wants: To keep Vụ Ẩn Môn out of every quarrel coming toward it: no tithe to Thúy Vi, no bargain with Tùng Đào, no robbers on his roads, and no one reading the pages but the man who buys them.
people.secret: Since 1190 he has sold Thúy Vi's Hall of Rules a list of what passes under the mist, a page each new moon, for patrols on the Đồng Sơn road and for Nhạc Chính Hành's silence on the tithe. He gets the lines by asking each road's keepers what every fee was paid for, as if for the accounts. Ký Thất Lộ carries the pages to the milestone by Đồng Sơn Trấn. Thai Vãn Xa's other carts are on the next one.

people.role: Road captain; a robber of Đoản Vĩ Cương once
people.appearance: A heavy, scarred man with a lynx-bone axe and a laugh that carries further than the mist he lays.
people.backstory: The fifth son of nobody, raised in the robbers' camp on the Ridge of the Bobtails. In 1081 a Thúy Vi road patrol ran him down on the Thạch Công road, and the founder Hàm Thủ Lộ (ham_thu_lo) hid him in mist and did not ask why (N-vu_an-02). He has guarded the road ever since. He formed his core in 1170, which puts him above his head in realm, and in thirty years nobody has asked him to lead the sect; a robber can guard a road, the cape says, but not own one. In 1190 his old band killed his friend Bối Trường Đình (boi_truong_dinh) on the Đồng Sơn road. Any robber he catches on the road he hangs by the boots from the nearest milestone and leaves for the carters to see.
people.wants: To die with his axe on a road he has made safe, and to see the boy he carried out of the caravan grow past his vengeance.
people.secret: At night he is learning his letters from a child's primer borrowed from Tập Mính Nhi, and tells the camp he is checking the tally.

people.role: The founder's daughter; keeper of the crossroads lanterns
people.appearance: A tall woman with ink-stained fingers who carries a green-paned lantern and looks at every stranger twice.
people.backstory: Hàm Thủ Lộ's (ham_thu_lo) daughter, born at the seat. She was forty-six when he walked into the mist by Đồng Sơn Trấn and was not found (N-vu_an-03), and for fifty-two years she believed Thúy Vi's Hall of Rules had taken the art back and her father with it. In 1198 the frost cracked the gate's threshold and her son found the bones under it: her father had died of age in Bàng Yên Tỏa's arms and asked to lie there. She has not spoken to Bàng since. She keeps every crossroads lantern on the cape lit, and still keeps her ledger of everyone who has called the Haze Walk stolen. She wants the founder's lantern from Bàng.
people.wants: The founder's lantern out of Bàng Yên Tỏa's hands, and her father's name cleared of the theft.
people.secret: She is teaching Hàm Tiểu Vụ the first steps of the Haze Walk in the lantern cellar, which the founder's oath reserved to the head, and Tất Hành Vụ lets it pass.

people.role: Mist-layer of the Phù Kiều road; on Tùng Đào's money
people.appearance: A neat woman in an undyed robe who smiles at everyone and remembers what they say.
people.backstory: Born in Phù Kiều Trấn, the river town the founder and Tất Hành Vụ (tat_hanh_vu) both came from. In 1192 her brother's gambling debts in Hàn Tân Thành were bought by an agent of Tùng Đào's first elder, Hồ Tùng Nguyệt (ho_tung_nguyet). The price of the debt is the Mist-Lock Lantern's key, the turning that lights any lantern on the cape, so that Tùng Đào's carts can lay the mist themselves. Each spring she holds the lantern while Bàng Yên Tỏa relays the gate's array, and she has learned two of its three turnings.
people.wants: To pay off her brother's debts and be a mist-layer who answers to no one.
people.secret: She has two of the lantern's three turnings and is copying the third off Bàng Yên Tỏa's hands each spring while she holds the lantern; Hồ Tùng Nguyệt's agent comes for it at the autumn fair.

people.role: Founder of Vụ Ẩn Môn (1050); the road guard who learned the Haze Walk
people.backstory: A carter's son from the river town of Phù Kiều Trấn and a road guard on the cape all his life. Tất Hành Vụ (tat_hanh_vu), eighteen years older, pulled him out of the river there as a boy, and they swore brotherhood when he came of age. In 1048 Tất taught him the Haze Walk (N-thuy_vi-07). He saw at once that mist laid like an array could hide a whole caravan, and he became a formation master at a hundred. In 1050 he founded Vụ Ẩn Môn to lay mist on the cape's roads and hide travellers from robbers (V015). He hid a robber once, in 1081, and never said why.
